rationale: ONTOLOGY/D25 — a constructor is not callable. A class body DECLARES; it does not execute ([class.mem]), and no member of a class may have the class's own name ([class.ctor]), so inside class `C` the only thing spelled `C` is `C`'s own constructor. In a WELL-FORMED class body the grammar agrees: `Direct();` parses as `declaration[declarator=function_declarator]` and the analyzer publishes a `constructor` symbol (pinned below). But a MACRO-DECORATED head — `class LIB_API Widget {` — is recovered as a `function_definition` whose specifier has no body of its own and whose PARENT's `compound_statement` IS the body, and that compound statement is in ERROR, so a bare `Widget(...)` inside it is recovered as `expression_statement > call_expression` or, under an access-specifier `labeled_statement`, as a `call_expression` inside an `ERROR`. The analyzer published `calls C -> C` for those: an edge asserting a class with no body calls itself. Measured over the two pinned C++ corpora (162 candidate files, 128 admitted as cpp by language-detection): 9 such rows over 6 files, each verified against its source line — `reporter.h:131` `BenchmarkReporter();`, `reporter.h:189` `JSONReporter() : first_report_(true) {}`, `state.h:172` `State(std::string name, …)`, `sysinfo.h:49` `CPUInfo();`, `sysinfo.h:61` `SystemInfo();`, `mutex.h:106` `MutexLock(Mutex& m) ACQUIRE(m) : ml_(m.native_handle()) {}`, `perf_counters.h:138` `PerfCounters(const std::vector<std::string>& …`, `perf_counters.h:154` `PerfCountersMeasurement(…)`, `benchmark_api.h:219` `FunctionBenchmark(const std::string& name, Function* func)`. Corpus `calls` 4,660 → 4,651 and relationships 10,348 → 10,339. The four `expectRelationships` rows are the OTHER direction and are what make the two `forbidRelationships` rows mean something: `Widget::measure()` calling `measure()`, `Plain::step()` calling `step()` and `MutexLock`'s member-initialiser `m.native_handle()` are all real calls and all survive, so the discriminator is `parentContext.kind === class` and NOT `source === target`. The last row pins that a well-formed class body never entered the branch at all.

expectSymbols.name: Widget
expectSymbols.note: the decorated head is published under its OWN name, so `calls Widget -> Widget` would have had a resolvable source and resolved to itself — the worst case for bb_graph's self-edge handling.

expectSymbols.name: measure
expectSymbols.note: CONTROL. A method whose body calls a method of the same name is a REAL self-call and the method symbol still publishes; a rule that suppressed on the spelling alone would delete this symbol's edge.

expectSymbols.name: constructor
expectSymbols.note: the well-formed path. `Direct();` inside a plain `field_declaration_list` parses as `declaration[declarator=function_declarator]`, so the constructor is published as a symbol and the analyzer never reads a `call_expression` for it. This row is what separates 'the guard suppresses a fabrication' from 'the guard hides constructors'.

forbidSymbols.name: LIB_API
forbidSymbols.note: the specifier's `name` field holds the MACRO on this shape family. Publishing the class under the marker would give the suppressed `calls` row a different wrong name, and this row makes that visible rather than incidental.

forbidRelationships.note: THE FABRICATION THIS FIXTURE EXISTS FOR, shape 1: `Widget();` and `Widget(int seed, int scale);` at class scope. A class has no body to call from, and a class cannot contain a member named after itself, so there is no reading of this edge that is true.

shape 2: the same declaration recovered one level deeper, under an access-specifier `labeled_statement` and inside an `ERROR`. A guard written for shape 1 alone would leave this row, so both shapes are pinned.

expectRelationships.note: CONTROL, the direction that costs symbols. `int measure() { return measure(); }` is a real call from a METHOD, so `parentContext.kind` is `method` and the guard does not fire. 43 `source === target` call rows survive over the same corpus and every one is from a function or a method.
CONTROL on a class whose head is decorated, so it cannot pass merely because the fixture's other classes are undecorated.

CONTROL on the SAME source line as one of the nine suppressed corpus rows: `explicit MutexLock(Handle& m) : native_(m.native_handle()) {}`. The member-initialiser carries a REAL member call and it survives, while the constructor's own recovered `call_expression` on that line does not. A guard that keyed on 'inside a decorated body' rather than on `source === target at class scope` would delete this row too.
CONTROL that an ordinary cross-class call is untouched.
